title: JIT Approval Token & Evidence Satellite — PRD sketch
summary: Sketch for a lightweight, just-in-time (JIT) approval token system combined with a customer-side evidence 'satellite' that records compact, privacy-preserving audit artifacts. Aimed at speeding customer-managed network onboarding while keeping auditable proofs for enterprise and compliance teams without shipping full log dumps to Redwood.
background: Problem: onboarding customer-managed VPCs and network changes currently stalls because security teams demand long audit trails and complex approval chains. Sending full telemetry to Redwood is a blocker for some FIPs and data residency requirements. We need a solution that 1) lets customers approve ephemeral operations quickly, 2) provides Redwood with verifiable, minimal evidence for compliance and incident investigation, and 3) preserves customer control over raw network telemetry.
audience: Primary: product managers and engineers building Private onboarding UX and operator flows. Secondary: Solutions Eng, SRE, Security/compliance reviewers at customers.
goals: JIT approval tokens that expire and can be scoped (time, CIDR, operator)
Compact evidence bundles emitted to a customer-side 'satellite' process that Redwood can request/prove without requiring full log ingestion
Enable rapid operator UX: sub-5 minute typical approval for low-risk changes with optional canary/rollback gates
Support cryptographic receipts (signed digests) for every approval decision
Minimize PII/telemetry surface sent to Redwood; default to hashed/aggregated artifacts
non_goals: Not a replacement for full SIEM/ELK log shipping
Not implementing a global PKI for every customer in V1
Not building offline forensics tooling in this PRD
requirements: REQ-001: Generate JIT approval tokens that encode requester, scope, TTL, and gate-level (e.g., 'network-edit:v1')
REQ-002: Token issuance through customer console or operator API; optional multi-signature for high-risk ops
REQ-003: Evidence satellite runs in customer-managed environment (container or small agent) and captures proof objects: action digest, operator identity hash, timestamp, canonical config diff
REQ-004: Evidence objects must be signed by customer key (KMS/HSM) when available and include a compact proof summary to Redwood (<= 2KB preferred)
REQ-005: Redwood API to request evidence bundle for a given approval token; customer agent serves only on allowed endpoints and enforces ACLs
REQ-006: Audit retention policy support knobs: short (30d), standard (180d), long (365d) — but customer controls where raw logs live
REQ-007: UI for approvers showing risk score, change summary, suggested rollback commands, and related historical evidence links
REQ-008: Graceful fallback where evidence unavailable: Redwood records approval metadata and flags for manual follow-up
REQ-009: Rate limits and quotas for evidence requests to control costs
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Demo of end-to-end flow: operator requests change -> approver issues JIT token -> operator applies change -> Redwood retrieves compact evidence and verifies signature/digest
AC-2: Evidence bundle size median < 1.5 KB for common changes (e.g., route add/remove, SG update)
AC-3: Token TTL enforcement verified across failure scenarios (agent offline, clock skew)
AC-4: UX shows clear escalation path when evidence cannot be retrieved
AC-5: Security review sign-off on cryptographic receipt format
telemetry_contract: Saved-to-Redis: approval events metadata (no raw packet data), per-token status (issued/used/revoked), request latency histogram. Evidence retrieval attempts tracked with outcome codes. All telemetry stored in tenant-scoped tables; PII hashed. Minimum retention 30 days in Redwood backend unless long-retention addon purchased.
privacy_model: Default to customer-controlled raw telemetry. Redwood only receives compact, non-reversible digests and signed receipts. Customers can opt-in to send richer telemetry for advanced analytics. Document data flow diagrams (TODO).
api_contract: POST /v1/jit-token -> {scope,TTL,requester}; returns token_id + signed_token. GET /v1/evidence/{token_id}?since=... -> returns evidence-bundle (signed digest, summary, timeline). POST /v1/evidence-hook: customer can push evidence proactively. Auth: mTLS + per-tenant API keys. Backwards compatibility: tokens are opaque strings so we can evolve payloads.
ux_flow: 1) Operator clicks 'Request VPC change' -> pre-filled form shows autosuggested scope. 2) Approver receives Slack/email + Console modal with risk summary and 'Approve with JIT token' button -> can select TTL and conditional canary. 3) Token delivered to operator (CLI copy or agent handshake). 4) Agent emits evidence bundle after change. 5) Redwood verifies and marks token closed. 6) If evidence missing, auto-escalate after X minutes.
failure_modes: Agent unreachable: Redwood marks evidence_missing and sends escalation to SE/CS
Clock skew >= TTL: token rejected — fallback path to reissue token
Customer key unavailable: agent falls back to unsigned bundle with local audit marker
Operator tries replay: tokens are single-use and include nonce; replay rejected
security_considerations: - Keys: support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and bring-your-own HSM later. - Signed digests prevent tampering; include canonicalization rules. - Protect token issuance API with rate limiting and 2FA for high-risk approvals. - Consider audit-only read-only tokens for third parties; never allow raw log export without explicit consent.
implementation_notes: MVP: implement token format as compact JWS with minimal claims; implement agent as small Go binary using existing redwood-connector patterns. Start with POST-pull evidence model (Redwood requests bundle) and later add push hook. Reuse existing telemetry schemas and tenant ACLs. Use feature-flag rollout to a subset of Dedicated customers.
open_questions: Q1: Do we require multi-signer flow for legal/regulatory customers in V1? (tradeoff: complexity)
Q2: How to canonicalize network diffs across cloud providers to keep receipts small?
Q3: Should we provide a 'simulated evidence' mode for demo customers?
Q4: SLA for evidence retrieval? (30s/5m/15m tiers?)
rough_timeline: Q1 - research + crypto format decision; Q2 - agent prototype + token API; Q3 - internal dogfood + UX polish; Q4 - pilot with 3 customers and iterate based on feedback
notes: Notes to self: talk to Solutions Eng about typical customer objections (legal wants raw logs), loop in Security for threat model. Add sample evidence JSON examples (TODO). Keep default UX friction low — most customers will pick short TTLs for developer velocity. Also consider a separate 'forensics mode' that temporarily expands evidence collection when an incident is declared.
related_work_and_refs: See older drafts: cust-vpc-change-simulator (file id), edge-admin-delegation experiments. Also reference cryptographic-approval-receipts PRD and operator-attestation notes for overlap. Link to Linear: PROD-1274.
final_thoughts: This approach aims for a middle-ground: auditable, minimal proofs that respect customer data ownership and accelerate approvals. Need to validate evidence size assumptions with real change samples from customer telemetry (action: request samples from 2 pilot customers).
